PS C:\Users\shlok>     Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned
Set-ExecutionPolicy : Access to the registry key
'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PowerShell\1\ShellIds\Microsoft.PowerShell' is denied. To change the execution
policy for the default (LocalMachine) scope, start Windows PowerShell with the "Run as administrator" option. To
change the execution policy for the current user, run "Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser".
At line:1 char:5
+     Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned
+     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : PermissionDenied: (:) [Set-ExecutionPolicy], UnauthorizedAccessException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : System.UnauthorizedAccessException,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.SetExecutionPolicyComma
   nd
PS C:\Users\shlok>

That error means PowerShell doesn’t have **admin privileges**, so it can’t change the **system-wide (LocalMachine)** execution policy.  

You’ve got **two options**, depending on what you want:

---

### ✅ **Option 1: Set it only for your user (no admin needed)**
Run this command **exactly as-is**:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned
```

👉 This only affects your user account, not the whole system.  
Perfect if you’re just trying to run scripts locally or set up a dev tool like Node, Python, or something similar.

---

### 🔒 **Option 2: Set it for the entire system (requires admin)**
1. **Close PowerShell.**
2. **Right-click PowerShell** → “Run as administrator.”
3. Then run:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned
```

That will apply the policy machine-wide.

---

### ⚙️ Quick check:
To confirm the policy was applied, run:

```powershell
Get-ExecutionPolicy -List
```

You’ll see all scopes (MachinePolicy, UserPolicy, Process, CurrentUser, LocalMachine) and their current settings.

---

If you tell me *why* you’re changing the execution policy (e.g. running a script, installing something, setting up a dev environment), I can tell you which option is safer and best for your case.
